answer:
For rewards $r_1,\ldots,r_G$, group-standardized advantages are $A_i=(r_i-\bar r)/(s_r+\epsilon)$. All-equal rewards produce no comparative signal. In common GRPO objectives, averaging each response's token losses by its own length changes the per-token weight of long versus short responses; reward-standard-deviation scaling separately changes weighting across prompt difficulties. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.20783)

Dr. GRPO analyzes these as distinct biases and uses a constant length normalization and removes group standard-deviation scaling in its proposed correction. “Token-level normalization fixes it” is too vague: averaging across all batch tokens and normalizing every response independently are different objectives.

Track correct/incorrect response lengths, truncation, reward variance, and gradient contribution by prompt. The exact loss reduction is part of the algorithm, not an innocuous implementation detail. [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.12948)
